chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Qutayba al-A'sha, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) taught me, saying: Say.

In the Name of Allah the Majestic! I seek refuge for so-and-so with Allah the Magnificent, from the biting insects and the venomous reptiles, and the evil eye, and the general [plague of creatures], and from the Jinn and the humans, and from the Arabs and the non-Arabs, and from their spitting, their aggression, and their blowing [of spells], and by the Verse of the Throne, then recite it.
Then you should say during the second time: In the Name of Allah! I seek refuge for so-and-so with Allah the Majestic, until you complete it.

key_terms.آيَةِ الْكُرْسِيِّ: The Verse of the Throne (Ayat al-Kursi)
key_terms.الْعَامَّةِ: The general multitude or plague of creatures

ai.seo_question: What is the specific dua for seeking refuge from insects and evil eye according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) outlines a comprehensive ritual for protection (isti'dha) against both natural and supernatural harms, emphasizing the recitation of Ayat al-Kursi as a central spiritual shield. The variation in divine attributes between the first and second recitations reflects the Shia scholarly understanding of the multifaceted nature of divine protection, addressing different layers of affliction from physical pests to metaphysical jinn and humans.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Quteyba Al A’asha who said, 
‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> taught me saying: ‘Say,

‘In the Name of Allahazwj the Majestic! I seek refuge for so and so, with Allahazwj the Magnificent, from the insects and the venomous (reptiles), and the evil eyes, and the generality (of creatures), and from the Jinn and the human beings, and from the Arabs and the non-Arabs, and from their sorcery and their rebellions, and their spells, and by the Ayat Al Kursy [2:255]’ – then recite it.
Then you should be saying during the second (time), ‘In the Name of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! I seek Refuge with Allah<sup>azwj</sup> the Majestic’ until you overcome upon it’.
en.sarwar: 5. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Qutaybah al-‘A’Sha’ who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) instructed me with this supplication:

‘In the name of Allah, the glorious, I seek protection for so and so with (the help of) Allah, the Most Great, against all small living things (vermin, insect, germs, viruses and so forth), the venomous things, evil eyes, plague, the evil of Jinn and human beings of Arabs and non- Arabs, against their sorcery, transgression and against their spell, with reading verse 255 of Chapter 2

and in the second time reading the above supplication say, “In the name of Allah, I seek protection for so and so, with (the help of) Allah, the Glorious One ... to the end of the above supplication.’”
